ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs and managers against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance national sanctions lists, and the OFAC SDN list; mandatory PEP classification and enhanced due diligence in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12, the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; screening must occur before the notarial deed is passed, upon any UBO change, and periodically during the business relationship; the low-risk standard commercial classification under the banking AML risk tier does not exempt the entity from UBO registration, adverse-media checks, source-of-wealth verification or ongoing sanctions monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official administrative languages are French, German and Luxembourgish under the Loi du 24 février 1984 sur le régime des langues. Corporate names may be formulated in any language that uses Latin script; non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into standard Latin script. The name must comply with public order and good morals, must not be misleading, and must be accompanied by the mandatory suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the initials 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL' on all corporate documents and instruments.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gestion de fortune / Conseil en placement
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal by the LBR/RCS or by the notary, the applicant may correct the name and submit a fresh availability request without penalty. A formal refusal may be contested before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg under the amended Law of 10 August 1915, or, where the refusal arises from an administrative decision concerning reserved or regulated words, by a recours en réformation before the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification pursuant to the Loi du 21 juin 1999 sur les procédures administratives et contentieuses. The applicant may also seek interlocutory suspension via référé administratif. In all cases, the applicant should first instruct the notary to issue a corrective name-certification letter to cure the stated ground of refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole establishment for the intended international tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory business. Initial incorporation may rely on a fiduciary's domiciliation address for the registered office, but the Law of 27 December 2019, Article 89bis of the LIR and the Luxembourg tax administration circular LIR n° 20/1 of 18 March 2020 require physical premises, local staff, decision-making presence, management meetings and operational autonomy in Luxembourg for tax residency and treaty access. The cross-border consultancy model demands verifiable commercial substance and transfer-pricing documentation capacity in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% per fiscal year probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Luxembourg tax administration, the Social Security Inspectorate, or the CSSF where a license is held; probability escalates when the entity claims treaty benefits and executes intra-group cross-border contracts without commensurate local staff and premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales); Title V, Articles 486–490 (SARL formation, capital and shares); Article 9 (registration with the Trade and Companies Register).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the online RCS portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Articles of Incorporation (Statuts) and the RCS registration form (Formulaire de constitution), file-stamped and published electronically.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL has a minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed at formation; at least 25% of cash contributions must be paid up and deposited into a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution, with release only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE FOUNDERS ACTING AS INITIAL BOARD: 1. The founders subscribe in full to 12,000 ordinary shares with a par value of EUR 1.00, representing the subscribed capital of EUR 12,000. 2. The subscription funds shall be deposited into a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg bank until registration. 3. The registered office of the SARL is adopted at its stated address in Luxembourg. 4. The initial managers are appointed with full powers to represent the SARL, operate bank accounts, and complete all licensing filings. RESOLVED FURTHER that any one manager may sign all RCS registration instruments and related administrative declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and availability verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS online portal (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request through the RCS portal or instruct the notary to process it; provide up to three proposed corporate names in descending order of preference; the RCS checks the name against existing registrations and reserves an available name for 40 days.
required_dossiers: Proof of intended registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a written appeal with the RCS registry officer within 15 days or promptly submit an alternative name with supporting evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Notaire), member of the Chamber of Notaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French-language Statuts and arrange a meeting before the notary; the notary verifies legal capacity, share subscription declarations, registered-office consent and escrow evidence; after execution, the notary prepares the deed for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID cards of shareholders and managers
Registered-office consent letter from the premises owner
Bank certificate confirming blocked capital escrow
Antecedent certificate of any corporate founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the statutory text and resubmit; execute a supplemental notarial deed before the same or another Luxembourg notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription deposit and bank escrow certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution licensed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company-in-formation; deposit at least 25% of the subscribed cash capital; obtain a bank certificate confirming the blocked balance and the account holder's identity for use in the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays the certificate, approach another CSSF-licensed bank or request the current bank to issue an interim escrow attestation in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the notarial deed, the notary e-files the deed and the RCS registration form through the LBR portal; pay the RCS registration fee; submit the required statutory information and receive the RCS registration number and extract.
required_dossiers: Identification sheets for managers and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, provide written explanations and supplementary documents via the e-registration portal within 10 business days; appeal to the registry judge if the application remains contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés (RES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary submits the statutory abstract for publication in the electronic compendium; the publication identifies the company name, registered office, share capital, managers and the RCS registration certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request the notary to expedite via the LBR portal and confirm the publication link within 24 hours; correct any typographical mismatches promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Luxembourg national business number and corporate income tax registration through the ACD; file the VAT registration application via MyGuichet.lu with the AEDT; obtain a Luxembourg VAT number and tax registration certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities query the application, supply the RCS extract and Articles of Incorporation; alternatively apply for late-report relief and follow up with the competent tax bureau.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with the social security centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL as an employer with the CCSS through MyGuichet.lu; enrol the managers and any employees; obtain the employer registration number and set up wage-withholding and social contribution compliance.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and residence permits of employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CCSS registration is delayed, obtain a provisional registration number through MyGuichet.lu and reconcile the final employer number once the file is cleared.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate-General for Industry, New Technologies, Research and Energy (Direction Générale de l'Industrie, des Nouvelles Technologies, de la Recherche et de l'Énergie)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for an autorisation d'établissement through MyGuichet.lu before commencing operations; provide evidence of managerial capability or professional qualification as required for consultancy services; await the formal ministry decision.
required_dossiers: Professional qualification certificates or relevant management experience proof
Criminal record extract (extrait du casier judiciaire)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused, request written reasons and appeal to the administrative court within two months; alternatively complete the missing professional requirements and submit a revised application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical premises safety and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a workplace safety inspection and obtain the fire-safety certificate for the registered office; arrange a structural load inspection of the premises; ensure compliance with occupational health and safety requirements before staff occupation.
required_dossiers: Fire safety certificate or CGDIS inspection report
Workplace safety arrangements and employee list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If clearance is conditional, remedy the identified fire or structural deficiencies and request a revised inspection within 30 days; maintain records until full clearance is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate-General for Industry, New Technologies, Research and Energy (Direction Générale de l'Industrie, des Nouvelles Technologies, de la Recherche et de l'Énergie)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 governing access to the artisanal, commercial and liberal professions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration category for tertiary office-based activity; full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required for ISIC 7020 management consultancy.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater of domestic quality may be discharged to the public sewage system (COD ≤ 125 mg/l, pH 6.5–9.5); no industrial VOC sources are present; electronic and packaging waste must follow the Luxembourg WEEE and packaging schemes; hazardous waste, if generated, must be carried with a Bordereau de Suivi des Déchets by an approved collector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate issued by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) after premises inspection; structural load report prepared by an approved civil engineer; and occupational workplace clearance issued by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) confirming compliance with Luxembourg work-safety, accessibility and office hygiene rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for value added tax. Primary electronic portals: impotsdirects.public.lu, guichet.lu, and MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL is automatically issued a national business registration number (NIF / matricule) upon incorporation via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and registration with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS). The SARL must then apply separately for a Luxembourg VAT identification number with the AEDT using the VAT registration declaration (Formulaire 1041/C), submitted online through MyGuichet.lu together with the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, RCS extract, proof of the legal representative's authority, and, where applicable, a copy of the client engagement letters substantiating cross-border services. For a foreign entity supplying taxable services in Luxembourg without an establishment, a Luxembourg VAT ID is obtained from the AEDT by the same electronic route; no local legal establishment is required, but a fiscal representative may be mandated for non-EU residents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box or multi-entity classification election. A SARL is statutorily opaque and fully subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), with no look-through treatment for Luxembourg resident owners. Limited statutory optionality exists under the ATAD implementation law of 28 December 2018 to elect hybrid-mismatch safe-harbor alignment, the group 75% participation-exemption regime, and the notional interest deduction on new equity. A Luxembourg permanent establishment may elect to compute its branch taxable base according to treaty-relevant allocation principles if consistent with the Luxembourg-Non-Resident tax treaty and OECD transfer pricing guidelines.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises under the simplified small-business exemption; no threshold applies for non-resident suppliers not established in Luxembourg, who must register for VAT as soon as they make any taxable supply of goods or services in or from Luxembourg, subject to place-of-supply rules and reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance, transaction-based reporting, or mandatory digital stamping regime as of the current year. E-invoicing is mandatory for B2G invoices through the national Peppol-based e-Lux platform (issued via MyGuichet). Domestic B2B invoicing may continue in paper or digital form, but structured formats aligned with EN 16931 are recommended. Luxembourg is expected to implement mandatory EU-wide B2B e-invoicing and digital real-time reporting upon adoption of the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package, projected by calendar year 2028.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Luxembourg SARL providing cross-border tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory services may benefit from an effective 0% VAT treatment when the service is supplied to a taxable business customer established outside the European Union. This follows the B2B place-of-supply rule (Luxembourg VAT Act Article 34, transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC Article 44), under which the supply is outside the Luxembourg territorial scope. For goods exported outside the EU, zero-rating applies at 0% if the SARL evidences dispatch from Luxembourg within 90 days and holds proof of transport out of the EU. Services ancillary to exported goods, transfer of licences, and financial facilitation services to non-EU counterparties are also outside the Luxembourg VAT net provided contractual and payment flows substantiate the non-EU recipient status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively disallow zero-rating or outside-scope treatment if the exporter cannot produce credible evidence of physical exit of goods or of the non-EU establishment of the service recipient. Penalties and consequences include: (i) reassessment of VAT at 17% on the full invoice value; (ii) late-payment interest at 5% for the first month and 1% for each additional month, capped at a total of 20%; (iii) administrative fines of up to EUR 12,500 for incorrect invoicing and up to double the evaded tax in cases of fraudulent intent; (iv) joint and several liability of the SARL's directors and designated VAT representative; and (v) a clawback prescription window of 5 years, extended to 8 years where concealment, fraud, or intentional obstruction is established. Export refund claims are routinely selected for risk-based documentary audits by the AEDT customs unit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full capital and current account convertibility as a eurozone member state. There are no exchange control restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, interest, or capital, provided that standard tax, AML/KYC, and statistical reporting obligations are satisfied. Foreign-owned SARLs may remit dividends and liquidation proceeds freely via the TARGET2 payment system, subject to beneficial ownership documentation and applicable withholding tax formalities under Luxembourg domestic law and tax treaties. No prior central bank approval is required for cross-border transfers, but intra-EU and third-country payments must be reported for balance-of-payments statistics under BCL Circular 2015 and related CSSF regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirements on export receipts. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, no prescribed timeline for repatriation, and no obligation to sell foreign currency earned from exports to the BCL or any authorized bank. Exporters may freely hold foreign currency accounts at Luxembourg credit institutions or maintain balances abroad, subject to OECD transfer pricing rules and the arm's length principle for related-party transactions. For tax purposes, export revenues are taxable in Luxembourg to the extent attributable to the Luxembourg entity under the territoriality rules of the Luxembourg income tax law (LIR), as refined by case law and administrative practice.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Legally feasible only through Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) or EU-passported EMIs registered with the CSSF. The viability rating is Medium for operational liquidity platforms and Low for capital escrow functions. Non-EU offshore digital EMIs are generally not acceptable for SARL corporate account opening because they lack a local or EU banking license, cannot clear through TARGET2, and trigger heightened AML scrutiny. Luxembourg-regulated EMIs such as PayPal Luxembourg, S.A. (if appropriately licensed) or other CSSF-passported players may be used solely for ancillary payment collection, not for substantial treasury holdings. Any use must be supplementary to a credit institution headquartered in the EU.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is generally required for the first in-person interview at the selected bank or a trusted domiciliation agent, although most Luxembourg banks have moved to hybrid remote onboarding for low-risk commercial clients. A joint physical meeting is strongly advisable for bank account opening, as banks are required to apply CSSF circular 12/544 provisions on anti-money laundering and risk-based due diligence. Remote opening is permissible in practice only when the client’s ultimate beneficial owners and directors already maintain a substantial relationship with the bank, or when the bank uses an EU-certified video identification solution coupled with electronic signature, but the final compliance decision remains at the bank’s discretion. For the purpose of this advisory, the mandate is High: an in-person or video-call interview with at least one director with signing authority is mandatory; the other non-signing director may be identified through certified copies of passports and proof of residential address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification incomplete or inconsistent with corporate register
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO declaration (Luxembourg form), sub-threshold ownership declarations for every shareholder, organizational chart with economic link to the SARL, certified passport copies of all UBOs, proof of residential address, and an excerpt from the Luxembourg trade register (RCS) confirming registered UBO filings under the Law of 13 January 2019.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or sensitive foreign jurisdictions for shareholders or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial substance documentation for any non-resident shareholder, tax residency certificates, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, group structure overview with operating entities, rationale for the Luxembourg entity, and any required sanctions screening clearance or FATF jurisdictional risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transfer pricing or zero-profit expectations from a consulting company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master file and local file pursuant to Luxembourg transfer pricing rules, TP policy with functional and risk analysis, economic substance memorandum, board minutes demonstrating strategic decision-making in Luxembourg, desk or office lease agreement, list of local employees or outsourced service providers, and budget projections showing arm's length remuneration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to high-risk countries or non-cooperative territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts and invoices for underlying services, beneficial ownership certificates of recipient entities, purpose codes, sanctions screening outputs, transaction-level business rationale, and any required prior notification to the CSSF or the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) for suspicious flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid capital injection followed by immediate dividend or loan distributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subordinated debt agreements, shareholder loan documentation, transfer pricing benchmark, tax ruling or advance pricing agreement if applicable, historical financial statements, board resolutions authorizing the flows, and evidence that the distribution is made out of distributable profits under Luxembourg company law and the SARL articles of association.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be transferred via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank account to the SARL's euro-denominated account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The wire must be titled 'Paid-in capital contribution' or 'Share capital deposit' and include the SARL's name and LEI (549300LUX) to facilitate reconciliation. The payment purpose code should be selected as 'Share capital injection into a non-financial corporation' under the ECB's Balance of Payments reporting (BOP) framework; in practice the bank will map this to code T110 or similar under the BCL's reporting schema. The contribution must be supported by (i) a notarized deed of incorporation or minutes of the extraordinary general meeting resolving the capital increase, (ii) a statement from the registered auditor or expert confirming the consideration is fully paid up, (iii) proof of the shareholder's identity and source of funds, and (iv) a bank certificate confirming receipt and crediting to the restricted capital escrow account, if applicable. The BCL statistical report must be filed by the receiving bank within the mandatory timeliness window (normally five business days). For injection in currency other than EUR, conversion must be executed at the prevailing ECB reference rate or a bank-offered spot rate, with conversion documentation retained for AML and tax purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments are settled primarily through SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for euro-denominated low-value flows within SEPA. For high-value or third-country trade settlements, an MT103 with full cover or an MT202COV may be used. Commercial letters of credit (LCs) can be opened through the Luxembourg bank's trade finance desk, using the UCP 600 rules; documentary collections are cleared via SWIFT MT798/MT799 sequences. For consulting services, the disbursement is typically an invoice settlement via MT103 or SEPA CI (Credit Transfer) with explicit reference to the invoice number, ISIC 7020 service description, and VAT treatment. The bank will require the underlying service contract, invoice, and AML/KYC documentation for the payee; payment purpose codes must align with the EU Balance of Payments statistic categories. Any disbursement above EUR 50,000 is subject to enhanced due diligence. The clearing rails must be compliant with Council Regulation (EU) 2023/821 (dual-use) and EU sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards executed with the SARL's Luxembourg credit institution under an ISDA or local master agreement, with mandatory tear-sheet confirmation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to convertibility restrictions, including BRL, INR, or CNY, traded through EU-authorized counterparties only
FX swaps for rolling hedging positions and repurchase side operations, executed with the same credit institution or an EU-passported broker
Vanilla FX options and call spreads used to cap conversion costs on anticipated dividends or capital repatriation
Cross-currency swaps or swaps with a combined interest rate and FX component, only where the underlying commercial exposure is documented
Money market deposits in foreign currency for day-to-day treasury balancing without speculative positions, subject to the BCL statistical reporting and the SARL's treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 7 months after the financial year-end; if the annual general meeting approves the accounts earlier, filing must occur within 1 month of approval. For a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may be penalized by a court order to file within a set term, daily penalties, and criminal fines against directors; persistent non-filing may lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, the SARL must file a declaration confirming that the registered UBO information remains accurate; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 1 month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes an AML offence: criminal fines up to EUR 1,250 and/or imprisonment from 6 days to 6 months; the company may also be subject to administrative removal of its RBE registration and consequential restrictions on corporate transactions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when, on its balance-sheet date, it exceeds at least two of the following three criteria: total assets exceed EUR 4.4 million; annual net turnover exceeds EUR 8.8 million; average workforce exceeds 50 employees. Small undertakings below these thresholds are exempt from mandatory audit unless the articles of association or a minority shareholder validly request one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) as set out in the Luxembourg accounting and annual accounts legislation; IFRS as adopted by the European Union is permitted for consolidated financial statements and may optionally be used for individual statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once per calendar year, the SARL must file a confirmation declaration with the RBE stating that the recorded beneficial-owner data remain accurate. The declaration must be made within one month after each relevant change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers; non-resident ownership is permitted and does not alter the underlying UBO disclosure obligation. The RBE information must be kept continuously accurate and traceable.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 per year for a standard Luxembourg domiciliation/registered agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 per year for a small SARL not requiring consolidated audit; higher fees apply where a full statutory audit is mandated

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate corporate tax rate in Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 7% unemployment surcharge on the CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax); in other municipalities the CIT plus unemployment surcharge is 18.19%, plus municipal business tax ranging from 6.75% to 10.50%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (effective combined rate approx. 4.98%); participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; R&D tax credit; investment tax credit; favourable interest limitation rules under ATAD with effective rate impact; zero-rate on qualifying outbound dividends under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward; annual offset capped at 75% of taxable income exceeding EUR 25,000 for corporate income tax and municipal business tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg CIT and municipal business tax return (Form 1200) submitted electronically through MyGuichet.lu with LuxTrust authentication; separate net wealth tax return (Form 1231) is required; VAT return (Form 2000) applies where VAT registered.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers, the completed tax return must be filed by 31 December of the year following the tax year; fiscal-year taxpayers must file within five months after the close of the fiscal year unless an extension is granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer name, address, Luxembourg RCS number, tax ID (matricule), legal form, and ISIC/NACE business activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign shareholders and beneficial owners with country of residence; no local registration needed for non-resident shareholders; the company must state its domiciliation in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Period covered by the return; reporting currency and exchange rates used if accounts are not maintained in EUR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities reporting through a Luxembourg permanent establishment must convert local books into EUR and attach audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Balance sheet and profit and loss data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All commercial balance sheet and P&L items, including depreciation, provisions, accrued interest and extraordinary items, tied to Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the statutory accounts to the tax return; disclose any foreign permanent establishments and their results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax adjustments and disallowed expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses (e.g. excessive interest, penalties, gifts), participation exemptions, notional expense deductions, disguised profit distributions and other tax law adjustments to commercial net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-parent intra-group fees must be arm's length; unjustified or undocumented management fees or interest are recharacterized as constructive dividends and trigger withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares the current-year taxable result and the amount of prior-year tax losses used; carryforward is unlimited in time, capped at 75% of taxable income exceeding EUR 25,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that shareholding and business activity tests for loss carryforward after acquisition of a controlling interest continue to be satisfied; a change in non-resident ownership above 25% can terminate loss carryforwards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Foreign income and international confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income, controlled foreign corporation inclusions, foreign tax credit calculations and tax treaty provisions invoked.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a valid Luxembourg tax residency certificate and a foreign tax credit analysis; disclose the non-resident ultimate parent for CbC and substance checks.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of EUR 100 to EUR 25,000, with higher amounts for repeated failure; automatic late-payment interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid CIT and municipal business tax; estimated tax assessments may be issued; false or incomplete returns can trigger criminal tax evasion penalties of up to EUR 125,000 fine and up to 5 years imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends paid by a Luxembourg resident company to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% or 25% participation test) or under an applicable DTA (often 0% or 5%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must complete the Luxembourg release-from-withholding-tax form (model 105 for dividends paid to EU/EEA resident companies under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive; model 106 for DTA relief), obtain a latest-resident-country tax certificate (Form 6166 or attestation de résidence fiscale) and submit it to the paying agent before the distribution date. The paying agent may be authorised to grant up-front relief; any excess WHT is reclaimable through the ordinary refund procedure within 3 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 0% for arm's length interest and royalty payments to non-residents; however, payments to a related company in an EU blacklisted jurisdiction may be subject to 20% WHT; treaty rates generally 0% for qualifying interest and royalties, and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive and Parent-Subsidiary Directive may apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local/Master File monetary threshold; TP documentation must be maintained upon request under OECD TPG and Luxembourg administrative circulars (LIR 56/1-56/2). Mandatory CbC report for MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000; the local file is an expected part of any TP audit of related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a Gulf-style ESR regime; instead, the general anti-abuse rule (abuse of law) and beneficial-ownership requirements make economic substance (local employees, premises, strategic decision-making in Luxembourg) an essential prerequisite for treaty relief, participation exemption, and tax residency certificates. Passive holding, financing and IP companies are audited for substance, especially in hybrid mismatch and interest/royalty flow structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing false tax returns, concealing taxable profits, omitting dividend or withholding tax, or issuing fictitious invoices to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 125,000 (or up to double the evaded tax in certain circumstances) plus imprisonment from 1 month to 5 years; the tax administration may also impose an increase of up to 50% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be prosecuted and personally fined or imprisoned; courts may impose a travel ban; the director can be required to pay the evaded tax, late interest and principal penalties from personal assets under the theory of faulty representation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / Late Filing of Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting the annual Luxembourg CIT/municipal business tax return, refusing to provide requested documents, or repeated unjustified delays.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine from EUR 100 to EUR 25,000; default assessment may be issued using estimated income; late payment interest runs at 0.8% per month on the assessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director may be held personally liable for the tax if the company's non-compliance resulted from a clear personal intentional breach; in egregious cases a travel ban may be issued during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating with minimal substance while deriving passive income through Luxembourg under a tax treaty; routing funds artificially through a Luxembourg conduit without local employees, premises or decision-making functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the Luxembourg entity for tax purposes, recharacterisation of income, denial of treaty benefits, standard reassessment plus interest; civil penalties up to 25% of the additional tax (or 50% when evasion is proven).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly established or operated a conduit without substance may be personally liable for resulting tax deficiencies and can be barred from acting as statutory managers by the competent civil/commercial court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing tax structuring services without a valid Luxembourg operating licence (agrément for regulated professional activities), failing to conduct client due diligence, or facilitating tax evasion for clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cancellation of the operating licence; fines under anti-money-laundering law up to EUR 1,000,000 for legal entities; criminal sanctions including imprisonment for the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face fines, imprisonment, and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies; travel bans can be imposed pending AML proceedings; the court may order confiscation of illegally obtained advisory fees.
